note: Authored to the phase-2 prescription. Assets: the piece's own generated artwork (v3 generation plates + the still-body cutout), embedded as data URIs — raw material consulted as evidence; the composition, timing, word layer, labels and transformations are this branch's own. NO caption-band element exists in the file (defect D1 answered by construction): narration text exists only as per-line word groups in planned negative space. The figure plate is NOT used — its centre is generation-damaged (smeared); the figure beat is re-cast onto the generational row plate (phase-2 record). The dusk plate is zoomed ≥1.15 so its damaged foreground band stays out of frame. The water plate's centre is generation-damaged (the mother's neck dissolves); the scene mutes it with her ground-shadow and a tighter frame — recorded at the element (eo-watershadow) and in the register (R-5), not hidden.
plate_form: The plate's absence, by construction: grep this scene for any full-width bottom text band — there is none; the words live in .words groups anchored per scene between y=430 and y=640.

elements.home: the stage container — every compartment lives inside it; the render captures this element alone

DAWN plate — the empty world of the question: peach sky, one tree, no animal yet. The opening card rides it; L1–L2 speak over it. Its emptiness is the suspension's visual (doctrine §3: the question stays open on screen)
HERD plate — the answer as population: living bodies everywhere. L3–L4 land here so the claim is shown before it is analysed
LION plate — door 1: the spotted antelope hidden in the grass, the lion passing. Word space is the pale sky; the grass holds the proof
ROW plate (first entry) — three generations standing in a line: the copy made visible. It enters exactly at the copy sentence inside L5 (T-copy)
WATER plate — door 2: the mother drinking, the spotted calf watching. The route's stage
ROW plate (return, closer) — the compression restates the pair over the generational line that performed the copy
HERD plate (return, pulling back) — scale: the pair at population depth; the zoom reverses (settles wide) as the thought widens

DUSK plate — the fatal rule's world: sunset band, distant herd, the still foreground. Zoom 1.15+ routes the plate's damaged foreground band out of frame (recorded repair); its push-in HALTS across the sting (performed stillness)
FINALE plate — the dawn returned: pink morning, the herd small on the horizon. The epitaph's bookend (the opening light, transformed) and the end card's world
The light dying — a dusk-deepening gradient that rises across the fatal rule and holds the sting, then releases as the finale crossfades in. A lighting transformation, not a cut

The route drawing itself — 24 dots appearing one by one from the calf to the pool across "copied by watching, and by walking it": the knowledge being copied is the thing drawn (the information made visible, in the format's label/graphic tradition). The dots fade out WITH the water plate — a transformation belongs to its scene

REPAIR, recorded honestly: the water plate's centre carries generation damage (the mother's neck dissolves into a smear with a floating fragment). The scene lays the mother's soft ground-shadow over the junction and tightens the frame (zoom 1.06→1.12) — the damage is muted, not erased; a plate regeneration is the real fix and stands in the register (R-5)
The pool's ripple when the route arrives — the destination acknowledging the path

THE STILL BODY — the piece's one true cutout (transparent, 1019×360): the spotted deer lying still, eyes closed. It fades in as the fatal rule speaks, holds through the sting, and leaves across the plain statement. The archive, dead — shown, not described
EARTH ONE bug, top-left inside the safe rect (x=100, y=262), content beats only — the lane's furniture, no flagship marks (the channels must not blur)
Opening card — the dawn plate + EARTH ONE + the title (the promise the epitaph pays) + the series line. 1.6 s, per format

End card — the finale held: NEXT — THE STORY WAS THE FIRST BACKUP + EARTH ONE + the series line. The named next thing, in lettering; the spoken carry (L13–L14) has already done the inviting — the card is the door's sign, not the door
